newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges 2 men misled investors, caused losses.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges 2 men misled investors, caused losses.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it has filed charges against two men alleging they lured at least 365 investors in an investment scheme that led to $12.2 million in losses.

In its complaint filed in federal court in Ohio, the SEC alleged Mark Gatch, 39 of Amelia, Ohio, and Henry Benjamin Schmidt, 63 of Crestview Hills, Kentucky, raised more than $19.5 million from investors in Kentucky, Ohio, Florida and other states.
The agency said Gatch and Schmidt misled investors by telling them they could expect to earn profits on their investment of four to five percent a month, based on past performance.
The SEC said Gatch, who was sentenced to prison on related criminal charges, also made false representations to the investors regarding his trading strategy and subsequent losses.
"Gatch concealed these losses, and maintained the illusion of trading profits, by using the funds of existing investors and new investors to repay principal and pay purported profits," the SEC said.

Schmidt was accused of assisting Gatch in the scheme through his marketing and sales work, an SEC official said, warning that investors should make sure they do business with registered investment advisers.
"This started out as a small investment club and quickly grew and grew and grew and got out of control," said Henry Klehm, the SEC attorney handling the case.
"By the time the scheme came to light, investors had lost approximately $12.2 million, including approximately $4 million that Gatch and Schmidt took for themselves," the SEC said.
Lawyers representing Gatch and Schmidt could not be reached for comment.
